title: Zero-Shot Weight-Space Programming Across a Difficulty-Graded Ladder of Two-Player Games
editor_models: '6 Luna High' via Codex (identity unverified by author)
domain: games (two-player board games and chess endgames)

headline_result.text: Hand-written networks are exact wherever a one-pass local check suffices, but collapse in full adversarial play: the two chess endgames fall from 84.9% and 100% at mate-in-one to 0.57% and 9.13% full-game success, and a two-ply search with the same evaluation beats the constructed networks in every game.
headline_result.quote: the two chess endgames fall from 84.9 and 100 per cent success at the one-ply tactic to 0.57 and 9.13 per cent in full adversarial play.

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: one construction per game in the main ladder; 6 further construction attempts; statistical rungs 10 seeds x 400 games

key_claims.claim: In the main ladder, the constructing model had full code execution and exhaustive-search tooling, and override tables of exact positions were solved offline and baked into the weights.
key_claims.quote: Track A gives the model full code execution, iterative testing against its own test suite, and exhaustive-search tooling during construction.

key_claims.claim: Against depth-3/4 alpha-beta search, both standard-board networks lost all 800 games each, while winning most games against a random opponent.
key_claims.quote: Against search, both networks lose every game in both seats, with no exception across 1600 games in total.

key_claims.claim: A tablebase variant of the chess endgame networks forces mate from every legal position, so the ceiling is on compact derivable circuits, not on what the architecture can represent.
key_claims.quote: The ceiling this paper documents is a ceiling on what a compact, hand-derivable circuit achieves, not on what the architecture represents

key_claims.claim: Claude Haiku 4.5 completed only 2 of 9 tasks and declined the rest using incorrect feasibility estimates.
key_claims.quote: Claude Haiku 4.5 completed two of the nine tasks in this paper’s scope and, for the other seven, declined to attempt construction at all

key_claims.claim: A verification-habit prompt addendum helped on no rung in a paired single-attempt pilot.
key_claims.quote: Table 10 shows no rung on which the addendum helped.

key_claims.claim: Five open-weight models up to 8B, tool-free, all failed on Nim; the 8B model set none of its own weights.
key_claims.quote: No arm reached a second block. All five stopped on Nim, the ladder’s easiest rung

limitations_stated.text: The search-depth curve was never traced; every comparison fixes one opponent depth.
limitations_stated.quote: The first is that the second axis of Section 3 was never traced as a curve

limitations_stated.text: Override counts are upper bounds from one tier vocabulary; only for Wythoff is no better vocabulary proved.
limitations_stated.quote: The second is that our own override counts are upper bounds produced by one tier vocabulary

limitations_stated.text: Cross-constructor evidence mixes attempts run by a collaborator and by the same process, with differing sample sizes and opponents, so it is read directionally.
limitations_stated.quote: which is why those results are read directionally.

notes_for_review: A single-author benchmark of write-from-scratch WSP on ten games with exhaustive oracle checks, replicate games at each rung, cross-model attempts and a preregistered open-weight round. The 'zero-shot' label is misleading for the main ladder: Claude Sonnet 5 had code execution and exhaustive search and baked solved tables into the weights, so much of the exactness comes from offline solving rather than reasoning about weights. The tool-free track shows the capability largely vanishes in small open models. Cross-model results use different opponents and sample sizes and are not directly comparable.
